text: Good morning. I am Pennington P. Ledger the Third. Accountant.
Exhibit A. A loading bar. Please contain your excitement.
Behold. A circle of fiscal responsibility. Do not eat it.
A rectangle, divided into equal pieces. Strictly for research.
Orange cats are counted. Green cats are not. Very orderly.
A hero's health, as a fraction. I find this rather violent.
Liquid assets. A beverage, measured with the utmost precision.
My telephone battery. Fractions tell me when to panic. Quietly.
Seven pictures. One number. Fractions help us see numbers.
Zero?! Nothing at all?! This is a fiscal catastrophe!
Zero. The most dreadful number. Fetch my smelling salts.
All of it! One whole! I may actually smile.
Every piece accounted for! Best day of my entire life!
Exactly one half. Perfectly balanced. Like my checkbook.
A mere sliver. Technically a number. Barely.
Hardly anything. I have seen bigger crumbs.
Less than half. I shall make a note of that.
Under half. Mildly disappointing. Like decaf tea.
More than half. Acceptable. Mildly acceptable.
Over half. My monocle is almost impressed.
So close to a whole. The suspense is unbearable.
That fraction can be simplified. How deliciously tidy.
Equivalent fractions! Same amount, different paperwork.
Improper! More pieces than the whole? Most irregular!
Zero pieces? Dividing by zero is strictly forbidden!
Twenty-four pieces maximum. Company policy. Very strict.
Negative pieces? We do not do debt in this office.
Drawing fractions is child's play. Now, the audit. Five cases. Show your work.
Case one. Which is larger: five eighths, or two thirds? Think carefully. I am watching.
Two thirds. Larger by one twenty-fourth. A tiny margin, but money is money.
Case two. Someone claims six eighths equals three quarters. Prove it. I am very hard to convince.
Each quarter is two eighths. Double the top, double the bottom. Approved.
Case three. The knight claims seven quarters of a heart. That is more than one heart! Explain.
One whole heart, and three quarters of another. Most irregular, but correct.
Case four. Someone ate one quarter of my pie. Then three eighths more. How much is left?
Five eighths eaten. Three eighths left. I shall be filing a complaint.
Case five. I drink two fifths of a boba every day. How much do I drink in three days?
Six fifths. One whole boba, and one fifth more. I regret nothing.
